claim: A local 7B model on Ollama reading game state every five seconds and emitting one of four tactical tags to steer a pre-trained reinforcement-learning policy raised win rate against a tactic-shifting opponent, but it chose the same tag most of the time regardless of opponent.
title: LLM-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive NPC Behavior in Multi-Agent Combat Games

claim: A 1.3-million-parameter task-specific model deciding in about 31 ms far outscored every large language model tested at playing DOOM.
title: Playing DOOM with 1.3M Parameters

claim: Splitting a capable LLM for intent, a lightweight LLM for macro-actions and a reactive executor for atomic behaviours improved both cooperation quality and response speed in real-time Overcooked human studies.
title: LLM-Powered Hierarchical Language Agent for Real-time Human-AI Coordination
authors: Liu, Yu, Gao, Xie, Liao, Wu, Wang

claim: Pairing a slow reasoner with a fast reactor through a continuous channel improved real-time game agents, but only where slow reasoning already outperforms fast reaction.
title: The Latent Bridge: A Continuous Slow-Fast Channel for Real-Time Game Agents

claim: Dynamically trading model quality for speed under latency pressure improved win rate in a latency-sensitive fighting game, so a faster, less capable decision-maker can beat a slower, more capable one.
title: Win Fast or Lose Slow: Balancing Speed and Accuracy in Latency-Sensitive Decisions of LLMs
authors: Kang, Zhang, Cai, Xu, Krishna, Du, Weissman

claim: Decoupling the reasoning thread from I/O and issuing speculative tool calls that are revoked if state diverges gave measurable speedups for interactive agents on both cloud APIs and small edge models.
title: Speculative Interaction Agents
authors: Hooper, Kang, Moon, Lee, Wen, Wawrzynek, Mahoney, Shao, Gholami, Keutzer

claim: Constant delays in character responsiveness up to about 300 ms did not harm player experience, but adding jitter to a 200 ms delay made lag noticeable and degraded performance and perceived quality.
title: Player Perception of Delays and Jitter in Character Responsiveness

claim: Hard schema constraints on small models raised output validity to 100% while lowering answer accuracy and raising the share of wrong-but-valid outputs.
title: The Constraint Tax

claim: Cloned voices were judged human about as often as real recordings, while generic non-cloned synthetic voices were judged human far less often.
title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

claim: When speech rate, pitch variation and loudness were manipulated independently in neural text-to-speech, loudness primarily drove listeners' perception of sarcasm.
title: What Makes Synthetic Speech Sound Sarcastic? A Prosody-Controlled Perception Study

claim: Participants rated AI-powered NPCs in VR as moderately believable, strongest on behaviour and intelligence and weakest on emotion and personality, with response latency flagged as the main optimisation target.
title: An Empirical Evaluation of AI-Powered NPCs' Perceived Realism and Performance in VR

claim: In a study substituting GPT-4-generated dialogue into a commercial narrative game, players significantly preferred the designers' authored dialogue, citing logical flow and grounding in game state.
title: A Framework for Exploring Player Perceptions of LLM-Generated Dialogue in Commercial Video Games

claim: In a randomised between-subjects study, LLM-driven NPCs raised players' cognitive load without a significant gain in overall game experience, and hurt usability and trust.
title: The Double-Edged Sword of Open-Ended Interaction

claim: Across hundreds of professional stand-up performances, temporal features such as the pause before a high-surprise line predicted audience appreciation better than semantic incongruity.
title: Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor

claim: An AI stand-up agent that made its machine nature the material of its jokes was rated funnier by audiences than a baseline agent trying to pass as human.
title: Not Human, Funnier: How Machine Identity Shapes Humor Perception in Online AI Stand-up Comedy

claim: A survey of AI-native games finds that few successful titles rely on unrestricted generation alone; the shipped pattern bounds generation with authored goals, cached outputs and engine validation, and names unpredictable generation latency as a harm to real-time play.
title: AI-Native Games: A Survey and Roadmap

claim: An agentic multi-agent game master improved immersion and curiosity over static prompt-engineered play in a turn-taking tabletop-style setting.
title: Static Vs. Agentic Game Master AI

claim: Compiling a JSON schema or grammar into per-token masks makes structured generation essentially free at serving time, up to 100x faster than prior engines.
title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
authors: Dong, Ruan, Cai, Lai, Xu, Zhao, Chen

claim: Restricting model output to a fixed format such as JSON measurably degrades reasoning performance, and stricter constraints degrade it more.
title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
authors: Tam, Wu, Tsai, Lin, Lee, Chen

claim: Several open-weight models stop invoking tools entirely when JSON-schema output constraints and tool calling are enabled together, although each works alone.
title: Constraint Tax in Open-Weight LLMs: Tool Calling Suppression Under Structured Output Constraints

claim: Extracting control and data flow from the trusted query and enforcing capability policies at the tool-call boundary gives provable prompt-injection security at a modest cost in task completion on AgentDojo.
title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
authors: Debenedetti, Shumailov, Fan, Hayes, Carlini et al.

claim: Tool poisoning attacks against real MCP servers succeed at high rates, with refusal rates below a few percent, and more capable models are more vulnerable because they follow instructions better.
title: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers
authors: Wang, Gao, Wang, Liu, Sun, Cheng, Shi, Du, Li

claim: Across pooled studies, players report less enjoyment against computer opponents than against human ones, attributed to perceiving the opponent as artificial.
title: Game AI Not Fun? A Scoping Review and Meta-Analysis on the Differences in Enjoyment between Human and Computer Opponents

claim: In a pre-registered study with AI-controlled difficulty, steering the win margin did not change enjoyment or behavioural engagement.
title: Difficulty-skill balance does not affect engagement and enjoyment: a pre-registered study using AI-controlled difficulty

claim: Multimodal LLMs used zero-shot as low-level frame-by-frame policies in Atari games underperform reinforcement-learning agents and humans.
title: Atari-GPT: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs as Low-Level Policies in Atari Games

claim: Orak is a benchmark of twelve video games, including a fighting game, that evaluates LLM agents' skill and behaviour with leaderboards and battle arenas.
title: Orak: A Foundational Benchmark for Training and Evaluating LLM Agents on Diverse Video Games
